comparison: Both address the absence of endogenous Pou5f1/Oct4 expression in mouse Müller glia (C35, C36, C49-C54). OpenEval provides comprehensive RNA-seq evidence across multiple datasets and conditions, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this finding as establishing the rationale for exogenous Oct4 delivery. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address expression of other Yamanaka factors (C38-C43) in Müller glia. OpenEval explicitly evaluates RNA-seq data showing Sox2, Klf4, and Myc expression, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this pattern as explaining why Oct4 is the missing factor for reprogramming. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, with peer review also noting C168 (priming hypothesis).

Both address Oct4-induced glia-to-bipolar neuron conversion (C7, C14, C62-C64, C160). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of immunostaining, lineage tracing, and marker expression data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding with all three reviewers confirming the conversion. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address the synergistic effect of Oct4 with Notch inhibition (C8, C85, C87-C88, C161). OpenEval evaluates quantification data showing significant increases in Otx2+ cells in Rbpj mutants. Peer reviewers explicitly emphasize this synergy as a key finding with specific percentages (24.3% vs 4.5%). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R4 addresses synergy in Notch1/2 double knockouts (C92-C93) showing increased bipolar cells (15.8% vs 6.6%). Peer R3 explicitly confirms this finding with the same percentages. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address loss of Müller glia markers during conversion (C58-C59, C79-C81). OpenEval evaluates this as part of comprehensive lineage tracing evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of transdifferentiation evidence, noting rigorous genetic lineage tracing confirms neurogenesis from Müller glia. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address Ascl1 expression during conversion (C60-C61, C82). OpenEval evaluates temporal marker expression patterns. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of mechanistic data without explicit discussion. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address bipolar cell subtype characterization (C66-C68). OpenEval evaluates marker expression showing Otx2+, Scgn+, Cabp5+ identity. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this characterization as part of the overall finding. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address the absence of amacrine/photoreceptor markers (C69-C70). OpenEval evaluates negative markers (Isl1, Nrl, HuC/D) showing specificity for bipolar fate. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this distinction as part of characterization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address minimal proliferation and EdU incorporation data (C71-C76, C89-C90, C162-C163, C183). OpenEval evaluates EdU labeling showing absence of proliferation-dependent neurogenesis. Peer reviewers implicitly accept low proliferation as consistent with direct transdifferentiation mechanism. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address scRNA-seq findings (C9-C13, C106-C114). OpenEval evaluates comprehensive single-cell analysis with UMAP clustering and differential expression. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the single-cell multiomic analyses as compelling, with all reviewers noting altered gene regulatory networks. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address scRNA-seq cell proportion data (C98-C102). OpenEval evaluates quantification of cell populations across conditions. Peer reviewers accept this as part of compelling single-cell analyses supporting main findings. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address chromatin accessibility changes (C151-C153, C158-C159, C167). OpenEval evaluates multiomic RNA+ATAC data showing coordinated gene expression and accessibility changes. Peer reviewers accept ATAC-seq data as revealing altered gene regulatory networks. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address Rfx4 identification (C11, C142-C143, C165-C166, C178). OpenEval evaluates gene expression and chromatin accessibility data supporting Rfx4 as key target. Peer reviewers explicitly identify Rfx4 as a key finding and potential mediator of Oct4-induced neurogenic competence. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address Klf4 upregulation in Rbpj-deficient glia (C147, C150, C155-C157). OpenEval evaluates differential expression and chromatin accessibility showing selective Klf4 induction. Peer reviewers identify Klf4 as a potential mediator of Oct4-induced neurogenic competence. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address mechanistic interpretation of Oct4 cooperation with endogenous factors (C115-C117, C164). OpenEval evaluates this as part of scRNA-seq analysis. Peer reviewers accept the proposed mechanism that Oct4 cooperates with endogenously expressed neurogenic factors to reshape Müller glia identity. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address the methodological strength of genetic lineage tracing (C160, C170, C174). OpenEval evaluates the comprehensive experimental design combining prospective lineage tracing with viral overexpression. Peer reviewers strongly emphasize this as a crucial methodological strength addressing field concerns about GFAP minipromoter specificity. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address selective AAV expression in Müller glia (C55-C56). OpenEval evaluates this as part of lineage tracing methodology. Peer reviewers emphasize the stringent GLAST-CreER system as crucial for avoiding artifactual effects from leaky viral promoters. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address the distinct mechanism compared to developmental neurogenesis (C175-C177). OpenEval evaluates comparative gene expression patterns and mechanisms across models, noting Rfx4 induction not seen in development. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this distinction as part of the novelty. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address endogenous Yamanaka factor expression priming cells for reprogramming (C168-C169). OpenEval evaluates this as a reasonable inference from RNA-seq data though without direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers accept that Oct4 cooperates with endogenously expressed factors. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Both address therapeutic potential claims (C15, C182, C184-C185). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative without functional validation or safety studies. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting lack of visual recovery demonstration as a weakness while Reviewer 1 acknowledges functional studies are beyond scope. Both identify this as requiring future work.

Both address reduced oncogenic risk from minimal proliferation (C183-C184). OpenEval evaluates EdU data supporting this safety implication. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as a logical inference from low proliferation data consistent with transdifferentiation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates claims about NFI factor requirement for GFAP promoter activity (C96-C97) as UNCERTAIN, noting limited coexpression data and alternative explanations not fully explored. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates claims about previous studies using GFAP minipromoters having confounding factors (C172-C173) as SUPPORTED based on citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers acknowledge this context when praising the genetic lineage tracing approach.
OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of Rfx4 functional role not being directly tested (C179) as SUPPORTED, noting this represents important future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates claims about Ascl1 effects on chromatin accessibility (C180-C181) as SUPPORTED based on citations providing context for Oct4's broader effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
